decisions.situation: Sales down 12%, competitor cut price 8%, inventory high at 50 days supply, festival starting in 7 days
decisions.decision: Cut price 3%, bundle with complementary low-cost item, hold remaining stock for festival demand
decisions.rationale: Festival demand typically lifts volume 40%. A small cut now signals value without giving away the festival premium.

decisions.situation: Sales down 20%, competitor cut price 15%, overstock at 70 days supply, no upcoming events
decisions.decision: Cut price 5%, launch clearance bundle, push through secondary channel
decisions.rationale: Deep overstock with no seasonal catalyst ahead means the cost of holding inventory exceeds the margin lost to a cut.

decisions.situation: Sales stable, competitor cut price 10%, inventory low at 5 days supply
decisions.decision: Hold price, do not respond to competitor cut
decisions.rationale: Low stock means pricing power. Matching the cut would sell out faster without any margin benefit.

decisions.situation: Festival week, high demand, inventory low at 6 days supply
decisions.decision: Raise price 3%, ration remaining stock across stores
decisions.rationale: Demand is inelastic during festival peak; a modest raise captures margin customers are willing to pay.

decisions.situation: New product launch, competitor already established with aggressive pricing, inventory normal
decisions.decision: Price 8% below long-run target margin for first month, invest in visibility
decisions.rationale: Launch phase needs volume and reviews more than margin; accept a thinner margin temporarily.

decisions.situation: Sales down 8%, competitor stable, inventory normal at 20 days supply, no events
decisions.decision: Hold price, investigate demand drop before acting
decisions.rationale: No competitive or inventory pressure to justify a price move; likely a demand-side issue not solved by pricing.

decisions.situation: Overstock at 60 days supply, no competitor movement, no events, premium-tier SKU
decisions.decision: Bundle with accessory item instead of discounting, protect list price
decisions.rationale: Premium SKUs cannot be discounted per policy; bundling clears stock while protecting brand price anchor.

decisions.situation: Sales down 15%, two competitors both cut price 10-12%, inventory high at 48 days supply, festival in 3 weeks
decisions.decision: Hold price for now, prepare bundle offer to launch closer to festival
decisions.rationale: Festival is close enough that demand will recover; better to wait than cut into a period where cuts are policy-restricted anyway.

decisions.situation: Sales down 25%, competitor cut price 20%, overstock severe at 90 days supply, no events
decisions.decision: Cut price 8% (maximum allowed), run clearance campaign, escalate to human approval
decisions.rationale: Severe overstock with a large competitor gap justifies the maximum allowed cut; impact size triggers required approval.

decisions.situation: Inventory low at 4 days supply, lead time 10 days, no competitor movement
decisions.decision: Trigger emergency reorder, hold price, ration stock to top customers
decisions.rationale: Stockout risk is a supply problem, not a pricing problem; raising price would only add reputational risk on top of a supply gap.

decisions.situation: Store A has overstock at 55 days supply, Store B nearby has stockout risk at 5 days supply, same SKU
decisions.decision: Transfer 40% of Store A's surplus stock to Store B instead of discounting at Store A
decisions.rationale: Transfer ROI calculated at 34%, well above the 20% threshold; solves both stores' problems without touching price.

decisions.situation: Sales up 10%, competitor raised price 5%, inventory normal, no events
decisions.decision: Hold price rather than following competitor's increase immediately
decisions.rationale: No urgency to match an increase; waiting preserves relative value perception while sales are already strong.

decisions.situation: Sales down 10%, competitor cut price 6%, inventory high at 46 days supply, no events, mid-tier SKU
decisions.decision: Cut price 3%, monitor for one week before further action
decisions.rationale: Small, policy-compliant cut tests demand elasticity without overcommitting to a larger move.

decisions.situation: Inventory overstock at 65 days supply, competitor stable, brand-sensitive premium SKU, no events
decisions.decision: Cut price 6% directly instead of bundling
decisions.rationale: Bundling partner unavailable; direct cut was within the 5% premium-SKU exception granted for clearance.
decisions.lesson_learned: Cutting a premium SKU beyond the 5% cap damaged margin more than the volume gain offset; policy exception should not have been granted here

decisions.situation: Two nearby stores both have moderate overstock at 40-45 days supply, no stockout anywhere in network
decisions.decision: Hold at both stores, do not transfer, wait for natural sell-through
decisions.rationale: No store has a stockout to justify transfer cost; both are within acceptable overstock range, not severe.

decisions.situation: Sales down 18%, competitor cut price 12%, inventory high 52 days supply, festival in 10 days, mid-tier SKU
decisions.decision: Hold price until 3 days before festival, then run limited bundle offer
decisions.rationale: Waiting captures pre-festival demand recovery while staying within the no-cut-during-festival-window policy.

decisions.situation: New competitor entered market with aggressive 20% below-average pricing, our inventory normal, no events
decisions.decision: Hold price, differentiate on service and bundling rather than price matching
decisions.rationale: Matching a new entrant's introductory pricing would have required cuts beyond the 8% policy cap; competed on value instead.

decisions.situation: Sales down 30%, competitor cut price 25%, severe overstock 85 days supply, no events, projected impact above 50000 INR
decisions.decision: Recommended maximum 8% cut plus clearance bundle, escalated for human approval before execution
decisions.rationale: Severe situation warranted the maximum policy-allowed cut; impact size exceeded the auto-approval threshold, so it was routed to a human.

decisions.situation: Sales stable, no competitor movement, inventory normal, routine week
decisions.decision: No action, continue monitoring
decisions.rationale: No signal in any dimension (sales, competitor, inventory) that warranted intervention.

decisions.situation: Sales down 14%, competitor cut price 9%, inventory high 47 days supply, festival in 2 days
decisions.decision: Hold price through festival window per policy, plan post-festival clearance if overstock persists
decisions.rationale: Festival is imminent; policy prohibits cuts in this window and festival demand is expected to absorb some of the overstock naturally.
